subject: MSA + Order Form: indemnity carveouts, insurance trigger & IP defense coordination

From: David Sherman <david.sherman@epotech.com>

Date: Sun, 8 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: indemnity redlines (IP carveouts & insurance triggers)

Soojin / Connor,

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form — our legal team has a few sticking points on indemnity that I wanted to raise before we get to signatures. I attached our redline (PDF) for reference. High level:

- We need an explicit carveout for third-party open-source components and commercial third-party modules that EpoTech brings into the deployment (we're not comfortable taking on their license risk).
- Insurance trigger: we ask that Redwood's indemnity (and any right-to-defend obligations) only kick in where the claim exceeds $250k or where Redwood is alleged to have materially modified the underlying third-party component. Otherwise, we want the claim flow to go through our procurement/legal teams.
- For claims related to AI-generated output, EpoTech wants a carveout for customer-provided prompts and downstream uses we control.
- Notice and evidence: please confirm a 30-day notice window and an identification/evidence list so we can triage.

We'd prefer Redwood to accept a narrower right-to-defend (Redwood can defend only for claims that arise from Redwood-supplied code or model changes). If Redwood insists on broad defense control, we need stronger proofs of insurer coverage and an explicit cost-sharing mechanism.

Can your legal team propose language that narrows the scope but still gives us a path to remediation? Happy to hop on a call if simpler.

Thanks,
David
David Sherman
Director, Contracts & Procurement
EpoTech Inc.

David — appreciate the clear notes and the redline.

Quick responses / proposal:
- Open-source / third-party modules: we can accept a narrowly drafted customer third-party module carveout limited to (i) components identified on a schedule and (ii) components for which EpoTech retains direct license/maintenance control. In other words, if EpoTech installs a third-party binary that we did not provide or modify, we will carve that out.
- Insurance trigger: we are open to an insurance threshold approach but suggest a lower trigger of $100k for claims tied to patent/third-party IP infringement so there isn't a procedural deadlock on smaller but material claims affecting operations. We can escalate larger claims through joint triage.
- AI output: Redwood's position is that model-generated output is covered by indemnity only to the extent it arises from Redwood-provided models or model customizations. We are comfortable carving out customer-provided prompts and downstream usage as you requested, with an explicit definition for 'Customer Prompt'.
- Defense control: our legal team (cc'd) prefers right-to-defend for claims that arise directly from Redwood's code/model; otherwise we accept joint control with explicit cooperation obligations.

I'll loop in Kimberly formally with the redline and ask for sample language. Connor — can you carry the commercial ask on the insurance for procurement? I will propose a short call with David and legal to align.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

David — thanks for the redline; I reviewed and drafted targeted language attached (proposed_indemnity_language_20270809.docx). Key points from legal:

1) Scope and open-source carveout
   - We will accept a carveout for third-party components that EpoTech (a) lists on a schedule at signing, or (b) expressly installs/controls post-signature. We cannot agree to a generalized open-source carveout that would eviscerate reasonable indemnity exposure for third-party claims where Redwood packaged or modified such modules.

2) Defense and control
   - Redwood proposes the following: Redwood has the right to assume defense of a third-party IP claim that alleges infringement of third-party IP by Redwood-supplied software or model modifications. If Redwood assumes defense, Redwood will (i) provide prompt written notice, (ii) have sole authority to control the defense and settle, provided that any settlement that imposes monetary liability on EpoTech requires EpoTech's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).
   - If Redwood does not assume defense, Redwood will reasonably cooperate with EpoTech and share costs on a pro rata basis where both parties' conduct contributed to the claim.

3) Notice and evidence obligations
   - We accept a 30-day notice window from the date EpoTech receives a claim. EpoTech must provide claim materials (complaint, infringement analysis, and any evidence available). Redwood will keep contemporaneous records and provide the same.

4) Insurance & trigger
   - Redwood can accept an insurance-trigger approach but we propose separate thresholds: $100k for patent/third-party IP claims (to avoid operational deadlock), and $250k for general indemnity breaches. Redwood will provide a current certificate of insurance on request; EpoTech should provide its insurer contact and cert.

5) AI output and customer prompts
   - By default, indemnity for model-generated output will exclude Customer Prompt content and downstream uses that are reasonably attributable to EpoTech's instructions or post-processing. We will include a definition of 'Customer Prompt' and exclude situations where EpoTech substantially modifies the model or integrates third-party content into prompt templates.

Please see the attached proposed language for inline comments. We're happy to take a 30-minute legal working session to clean this up and produce a final redline. If you prefer, we can provide both conservative and compromise clauses to choose from.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Soojin — appreciate the detailed draft and the split thresholds. A couple of quick pushes back from our side:

- We are hesitant to accept a $100k trigger for patent claims. Patent suits are expensive to defend and we prefer keeping the threshold at $250k as a practical matter.
- On defense control: EpoTech's preference is that Redwood retains defense control (if Redwood wants it) but Redwood must bear defense costs when it assumes control, and any settlement with an admission of fault requires EpoTech's consent. The pro rata cost share sounds reasonable where both parties contributed.
- For AI output: we can agree to the 'Customer Prompt' carveout but want explicit examples added to the definition so there is less ambiguity (sample: templated user prompts generated by our workflow engine; attachments will include sample prompts).

Let's do the short legal working session — can you share availability? We can have our counsel (cc'd) join.

Thanks,
David
